newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle brisk at $71, up $1 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle brisk at $71, up $1 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded at $71.00 per cwt in active trading, up $1.00 from last week, bolstered by light finished cattle supplies, according to feedlot sources.
About 30,000 to 35,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 20,000 to 25,000 traded in Kansas, the feedlot sources said.

Gains were powered by the tight availability of cattle on feed long enough to grade choice, they said. Tight supplies were a result of light placements early this summer and the pulling forward of cattle to be sold ahead of schedule.
Support also was tied to ideas that packers were ensuring they had live inventory to fill previously booked beef orders, the market sources said.

Strength was enhanced by projections for moderate to strong retail buying this week to replace beef sold during the weekend, they said. Retail demand also was attributed to sentiment that beef would be featured in promotions, along with turkeys and hams, for the Thanksgiving Day holiday in a little more than four weeks, the market sources said.
